newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's corporate watchdog confirms break-in.
newsitem.headline: Australia's corporate watchdog confirms break-in.

text.p: Australia's corporate watchdog, the Australian Securities Commission (ASC), on Tuesday confirmed that its Melbourne offices were broken into at the weekend.

However, a spokesman declined to comment on a newspaper report that the intruders were looking for documents on an investigation involving the nation's biggest retailer, Coles Myer Ltd. The ASC is investigating a 1990 transaction which cost Coles Myer A$18 million and benefitted a company associated with former chairman Solomon Lew by a similar sum.
Australian Federal Police (AFP) are investigating the incident. "I can confirm there was a break-in at the weekend but that's about it," said ASC spokesman Steven Blaney.
"We really cannot say anything until the AFP's investigation has occurred," he told Reuters.
